segments.text: THus much of the argument of relation: now let vs proceede• It is further said, Our father. And he is so tearmed, because he is the father of Christ by nature; and in him the father of euery beleeuer: yea of the whole bodie of the Church.

Quest. Whether may it be lawfull for vs in praier to say, not our father, but my father? Ans. A Christian may in priuate praier say, My father. This is warranted by the example of our Sauiour, Matth. 26.•9. O my father if it be possible, let this cup passe from me. And Math. 27.46. My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me? And Thomas praied, My Lord, and my God. And Paul, I giue thanks to my God, &c. And Gods promise is, Ier. 3.19. Thou shalt call me my father. The meaning of Christ is not to binde vs to these words, but to teach vs that in our praiers we must not haue regard to our selues onely, but also to our brethren, and therefore when we pray for them in our priuate praiers as for our selues, we put in practise the true meaning of these words.
